chapter: Sidemen, the Hampton years, race and money
title: Nobody black has made money except Duke
summary: Mingus says no black man is a millionaire and Ellington did not make money from Columbia; Johnson cites Famous Amos.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: And Erroll Garner?
Well, Earl Gardner --
Nobody made no money, man.
Huh?
I don't know any black man that made any money, except for the Duke, as a composer.
Yeah, but I don't know how you can say that, Charles.
The Duke told me, man, he didn't make no money from Columbia.
Well, that's relatively speaking. As I say --
A lot of writeups. Duke got a lot of writeups. He told me that. A lot of writeups, a lot of publicity.

Because I just think they steal from everybody, so that it's the system, and if you're an artist and you're assigned to a record company, that you're going to get shit on. You're going to get bad counts, you're going to get every -- they stick everything but the kitchen sink as an expense on your records. There's no way you can pay off a date, particularly if you're going to make records that have --
That's racial. I don't know any black man in America that's a millionaire. Do you know anybody that is? Black men are not supposed to have money. In Harlem, the dollar is worth 15 cents.
Yeah, but Harlem is a very, very, very specific kind of --
It's not just in Harlem, 125th Street. Harlem is a color. Black people trying to make a living.
Well, --
They don't pay you no money, man.
I know a -- I just know a black man who became a millionaire in the last year.
Got a couple of millionaires. I read
about them.

Famous Amos. Famous -- shit, here's a guy who made Chocolate Chip Cookie, and was very astute about packaging it and selling it. He put his picture on the cover and he sells a million dollars of chocolate chip cookies.
You're talking about a guy who did it himself, right? I'm talking about people who are employed by white people.
Nobody who's employed by anybody becomes a millionaire. That's not the way you get to become a millionaire.
Joan -- what's her name, Joan what? $600,000 per record? Joni Joanie Mitchell makes money.
Yeah, but Joanie Mitchell is -- again, --
